comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I suspect that the writes are going like this -> 500kb = 8 x 60kb parts data and 8 x parity. 16 IO + overheads. Likely 1-2 IO per drive per client S3 put. You will see only 8-10MB/s of client IO with 250 IOPS HDDs. Small files and wide erasure coding isn't very good for performance.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I'm not a minio dev - so do your own research.

but, I've seem better performance with:

echo "write through" | sudo tee /sys/block/<YOUR DRIVE HERE>/queue/write_cache
You would want to turn off the drive caches with hdparm also to ensure the consistency of the data.

Let me know if you use it and it helps.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Bypassing fsync disables all consistency guarantees.

Just for anyone reading. A power failure/crash will mean you will end up in confirmed object being unreadable. We will not recommend nor support setups with this.

Furthermore this will only work until the cache is filled. So you will have n minutes running very fast, but then suddenly performance will tank if the hardware cannot keep up. 

Closing. You are hitting hardware limits. There isn't anything we can do about that.
